Marcus Ade (customer C-200) has emailed about order O-2003. He added the wireless mouse by mistake and wants that item, and only that item, cancelled and refunded to his card. The rest of the order should still ship as planned.
</task>

You are the planning step. You have no tools here: think the task through and write the plan only.

Produce an ordered list of at most 8 steps for an executor who will have the full toolset. Each step must be one concrete action, specific enough to carry out without guessing, and must include any check that has to happen before it. Add a short rationale for the approach.

toolInput.rationale: Order state must be checked before acting, since the wireless mouse line can only be cancelled (per policy) if it hasn't shipped yet, and the refund amount must match exactly what was paid for that line. Cancelling releases stock that must be restocked separately, and the refund must go to card since this is an unshipped-line cancellation, not a return.
steps: Call get_order for O-2003 to view all lines, confirm which line is the wireless mouse, its lineId, quantity, amount paid, and confirm it has not shipped yet.
If the wireless mouse line has already shipped, stop and report to the user that it cannot be cancelled per policy (only returned), since the request is for cancellation only.
Call cancel_order on O-2003 with lineIds set to only the wireless mouse line's id, leaving all other lines untouched so the rest of the order still ships.
Call restock_item for the wireless mouse's productId and the exact quantity that was on the cancelled line, referencing orderId O-2003.
Call refund_order on O-2003 with lineIds set to the wireless mouse line's id, amountCents equal to the exact amount paid for that line (from step 1), and method=card.
Confirm via get_order on O-2003 that the mouse line shows as cancelled and refunded, and that all other lines remain active/unaffected.
